France completes test of new nuclear-capable missile
subhead: France's armed forces test-fired a new M51.3 nuclear-capable ballistic missile in the Atlantic Ocean on Tuesday, the defense ministry said. President Emmanuel Macron said the test 'demonstrates the credibility' of France's nuclear deterrent.

title: Despite pain, two former October 7 Hamas hostages promote message of peace
subhead: Among the 251 Israelis taken captive by Hamas on October 7, 2023, Aviva and Keith Siegel chose to speak publicly about the abuse they suffered. While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed the release of hostages as an achievement in his election campaign, the couple in their 60s has continued to oppose the war.

title: Cheikh Hamidou Kane, voice of Senegalese history, has died
subhead: A writer, statesman and minister several times over, Cheikh Hamidou Kane was both a major witness to and a participant in Senegal's contemporary history. He died in Dakar on October 3, at 98 years old.

title: On Cornell's campus, 'everyone is outraged' by the handling of gang rape case
subhead: While she was still a student, a young woman claimed that she was drugged and raped by seven members of a fraternity at the Ivy League university. Many students feel that the alleged perpetrators were not punished severely enough. In September, the plaintiff took her case to the New York State Supreme Court.

title: Anna Politkovskaya: The journalist killed 20 years ago for understanding Putin before anyone else
subhead: Murdered in 2006 in the stairwell of her apartment building in Moscow, the renowned Russian reporter relentlessly warned, with remarkable clarity, about the true nature of Vladimir Putin. Her reporting from Chechnya already foreshadowed the war in Ukraine.
